title: Cooling freshly cooked food
about: Times the two cooling stages for a batch of freshly cooked food and says what to do at each limit.

sources.name: MPI Yellow Card S39-00002, Cooling freshly cooked food

audience: Food business staff using an MPI food control plan

lines.text: Start this when the cooked food has dropped to 60°C. The 6-hour clock runs from now.

quotes.text: When cooling freshly cooked food it must get from:

lines.text: Use any of these methods, or a combination:

quotes.text: Use any (or a combination) of these methods:

lines.text: Shallow containers

quotes.text: placing your food into shallow containers

lines.text: Ice bath
Smaller portions

quotes.text: separating your food into smaller portions

lines.text: Blast chiller

quotes.text: placing your food in a blast chiller

reminders.text: 6-hour limit: food not at 5°C or below now must be thrown out

quotes.text: 60°C to 5°C (or below) in less than 6 hours or it must be thrown out

steps.title: Stage 1: cool to 21°C or room temperature

lines.text: Cool the food to room temperature or 21°C, whichever is colder, within 2 hours.

quotes.text: 60°C to room temperature or 21°C (whichever is colder) in less than 2 hours

lines.text: The whole cool-down, from 60°C to 5°C or below, must take less than 6 hours.

quotes.text: 60°C to 5°C (or below) in less than 6 hours or it must be thrown out

ask.question: Has the food reached room temperature or 21°C (whichever is colder)?

lines.text: The food did not reach room temperature or 21°C within 2 hours.
The card does not say what to do in this case. Follow your food control plan or ask your supervisor.
Gap in the guideline: the card states the 2-hour limit but gives no action if it is missed (only the 6-hour "thrown out" rule).
Put the food in the fridge.
From the card's "Check" section ("refrigerate once at room temperature or 21°C"); its exact words were not available, so there is no quote.
Cool from room temperature or 21°C to 5°C or below within 4 hours.

quotes.text: then room temperature or 21°C (whichever is colder) to 5°C (or below) in less than 4 hours.

ask.question: Is the food at 5°C or below?

lines.text: Food that has not reached 5°C or below within 6 hours of starting must be thrown out.

quotes.text: 60°C to 5°C (or below) in less than 6 hours or it must be thrown out

lines.text: The "6-hour limit" bar at the top shows how long is left.
Possible contradiction: stage 2 allows 4 hours, but if stage 1 was quick the 6-hour total may not yet be up. The card does not say which limit wins.
Keep the food cooling in the fridge. The "6-hour limit" bar at the top shows how long is left.
No new 4-hour timer here: the 4 hours already ran out, and the 6-hour limit is the one left to apply.

ask.question: Is the food at 5°C or below?

options.label: No, and the 6-hour limit is reached

lines.text: Throw the food out.

quotes.text: 60°C to 5°C (or below) in less than 6 hours or it must be thrown out

lines.text: Record what was thrown out and why.
The food is cooled. Keep it at 5°C or below.
Record the food, the date it was cooked and how long it took to cool. (The Log tab has the times.)
